results.label: the parent tree IS the committed 67f2ed2 M112 release: it HAS the review artifacts of M99/M101 and no period ruler of its own
the delivered tree creates exactly the parent’s schema: every table, index and trigger is byte-identical DDL, so this milestone adds no schema object of any kind
and on the same fixture every table is byte-identical, the review table included — the periods and the coverage store nothing new
the review table the coverage reads has exactly the columns the parent declared, so a period cannot be addressed by a column this milestone invented
the PARENT’s own code reads the seeded artifact as a completed review, so the delivered tree is interpreting a legal row rather than a fixture shape
and the parent’s own payload has NO period series and no period record — the absence this milestone closes, measured in the parent’s code rather than asserted about it
the delivered tree reads the parent’s OWN file and reports the same period on the review calendar: the week of 2026-10-05
the weekly and quarterly buckets are derived from the closes the parent wrote, and the quarter the closes fall in is named
the artifact the parent’s own module wrote is joined to that period as `completed`, with its id and focus intact
the periods the parent never reviewed are `not_recorded`, and the period still running is counted as open rather than skipped
reading the periods on the parent’s file changes NOTHING: every table’s digest is identical before and after the read
the record’s limits are the ones a review needs: read-only, zero writes, no grade/cap/permission/plan-change influence, nothing causal
the parent’s own code still opens the file afterwards and sees exactly the artifact it left: one review, completed, with no row this milestone added

scope: M13/M65 migration: no schema object added, and the parent’s own file is read untouched: actual runtime/auth/SQL/HTTP with a frozen UTC clock, a synthetic calendar fed through the app's own parser and a patched market module for the thrown-read path; M111 calendar-read states (blocked/clear/unknown), no provider/broker/pixel/human proof and no claim about what a release does to price
